# 1 Clement Chapter 35 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_035_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 35

**35:1** How blessed and wonderful are God's gifts, dear friends! Life in immortality, radiance in righteousness, truth spoken with boldness, faith with full assurance, self-control in holiness — and all of this is within our grasp.

**35:2** So what are the things prepared for those who wait for him? Only the Creator and Father of the ages, the All-holy One, knows their greatness and beauty.

**35:3** Let us therefore strive with everything we have to be found among those who wait for him, so that we may receive a share in what he has promised.

**35:4** But how will this happen? Only if our mind is anchored in God through faith; if we seek out what pleases and satisfies him; if we live according to his faultless and holy will; and if we walk the path of truth, throwing far from us all injustice and wrongdoing, greed and quarreling, malice and deception, gossip and slander, hatred toward God, arrogance and conceit, empty pride and lack of hospitality.

**35:5** Those who practice these things are detestable to God — and not just those who do them, but those who applaud them as well.

**35:6** For scripture says: "God said to the sinner: What business do you have reciting my laws and claiming my covenant as your own?

**35:7** You hate to be taught, and you've tossed my words aside. When you see a thief, you join right in, and you make friends with adulterers. Your mouth is full of evil, and your tongue spins lies. You sit around bad-mouthing your brother, spreading rumors about your own family.

**35:8** You did all this and I said nothing — and you thought, you wicked one, that I was just like you. But I am going to call you out and lay the charges right in front of you.

**35:9** Think about this carefully, you who have forgotten God — before he tears you apart like a lion, with no one to rescue you.

**35:10** Offering praise is what truly honors me — and that is the path by which I will show him God's salvation."

---

*PNEUMA renders the Psalm 50/49 citation with strong contemporary rhetorical force, capturing the direct confrontational style of the divine speech.*
